methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $36M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Hystar is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Alejandro Oyarce Barnett that has raised $36M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private frontier-tech companies and 1 public peer (LNZA), spanning battery materials, hydrogen, and adjacent energy transition segments.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, which uses total capital raised as a proxy for current valuation and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yields $68M. Peer-median analysis identifies three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—KoBold Metals ($3.0B Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B Series C), and Amogy ($700M Series C)—producing a median valuation of $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M to $3.0B.

The triangulated range across both methods is $58M to $1.1B, with a median of $534M. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty inherent to early-stage frontier-tech valuation: stage-progression relies on backward-looking capital efficiency, while peer-median is sensitive to heterogeneity in technology maturity, market addressability, and capital intensity across the comparison set. The peer range itself ($700M–$3.0B) underscores this dispersion. Resolution of this uncertainty will depend on operational progress, capital requirements, and clearer signals on technical or commercial differentiation relative to the peer cohort.
